node-1.label: Patient had fever and left shoulder pain, and was found to have pericardial effusion

node-2.label: 14-year-old male, weighing 45 kg, was transferred to our clinic after pericardial effusion was found at a provincial hospital

node-3.label: Initial symptoms included fever and left shoulder pain

node-4.label: Physical examination revealed reduced cardiac sound intensity and elevated heart rate

node-5.label: The patient did not exhibit arthralgia or abdominal pain at any point during the clinical course

node-6.label: Three weeks before this event, the patient had an upper respiratory tract infection treated with ibuprofen

attrs.why: Both the laboratory physician and the radiologist independently favor an infectious process, specifically bacterial pericarditis, based on fever, moderate pericardial effusion, leukocytosis with neutrophilia, markedly elevated CRP/ESR, and PR depression/ST elevation, together with negative TB, viral, and ANA tests. This convergent specialist agreement and the exclusion of autoimmune, drug, and tuberculous causes strengthen the infectious pericarditis hypothesis, raising confidence from 0.86 to 0.87; pericardial fluid culture, blood culture, and procalcitonin remain pending.

Expert analysis excludes autoimmune causes and supports infection; negative ANA and absence of arthralgia/abdominal pain argue against systemic inflammatory disease. NLRP12 mutation and IL-1β elevation are nonspecific. Confidence decreased from 0.15 to 0.08.

Expert analysis excludes TB and no neoplastic features are present; negative TB tests and absence of weight loss/night sweats argue against neoplastic/TB effusion. Confidence decreased from 0.03 to 0.02.
Expert analysis excludes drug causes; no drug-reaction evidence is present, and infection better explains the findings. Confidence decreased from 0.04 to 0.01.

node-12.label: CRP level is 131 and ESR is 72

node-13.label: ECG shows PR depression and ST elevation

node-14.label: Tests for tuberculosis, viral infection, and antinuclear antibodies are negative

node-15.label: NLRP12 mutation is detected and IL-1β level is 10 pg/mL

node-16.label: Pericardial effusion is moderate in size

attrs.why: The neutrophilic leukocytosis (WBC 19,670/µL), high CRP/ESR, moderate effusion with ECG PR depression/ST elevation, recent upper respiratory infection, and negative viral/TB/ANA studies are consistent with bacterial pericarditis, and both the laboratory physician and the radiologist endorse this as the most likely diagnosis. Confidence increased from 0.62 to 0.65, still limited because pericardial fluid culture, blood culture, and procalcitonin have not yet identified an organism.
Expert analysis supports bacterial rather than viral etiology and notes negative viral tests. Recent URI and ECG changes are nonspecific. Confidence decreased from 0.28 to 0.12.
Expert analysis supports probable bacterial pericarditis and no Mycoplasma-specific evidence is available. Recent URI could fit but is insufficient. Confidence decreased from 0.10 to 0.05.
Expert analysis excludes TB; negative TB tests and absent weight loss/night sweats argue against tuberculous pericarditis. Confidence decreased from 0.05 to 0.02.

A recent upper respiratory tract infection preceded the fever and pericardial effusion, and both experts support a probable bacterial pericarditis on the basis of the neutrophilic inflammatory profile, high CRP/ESR, and moderate effusion. This post-URI temporal relationship makes a post-upper-respiratory-infection bacterial pericarditis plausible, raising confidence from 0.50 to 0.52 pending organism confirmation.
